morphemes.history: An (peace) is one of the most common auspicious naming syllables across the north and centre.
Bình (peace/calm) blankets old administrative names — a Confucian wish embedded in geography.
Phú (wealth) names prosperous townships, dense around the deltas.
Long (dragon) signals imperial prosperity; think Thăng Long, the ascending dragon.
Vĩnh (eternal) is a classic administrative prefix wishing permanence on a place.
Đại (great) marks places named for grandeur or seniority.
Tân (new) traces the Nam tiến — the centuries-long southward expansion stamping 'new' on fresh land.
Đông (east) — one of the four cardinal naming syllables.
Tây (west) — cardinal direction in administrative names.
Nam (south) names the southern reaches; also 'Việt Nam' itself.
Bắc (north) — cardinal direction, dense in the northern provinces.
Hà (river, Sino-Vietnamese) — Hà Nội, 'inside the rivers'.
Sơn (mountain) names the uplands and mountain districts.
Thủy (water) appears where water defines the place.
Giang (river, SV) is the larger-river twin of Hà.
Hải (sea) marks coastal places — Hải Phòng, the sea-defence.
